title: The larger event came first in 81 of 112 close deep earthquake pairs in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested magnitude order in deep earthquake pairs in a fixed global ComCat snapshot for 2000-2025. Both events had depth greater than 300 km and preferred magnitude at least 5.5. Primary pairs were within 200 km chord distance and seven days, with a magnitude gap of at least 0.3. The larger event came first in 81 of 112 pairs (72.3%). A conditional 95% component bootstrap interval was 60.0-85.3%. The exact two-sided probability was 0.000352 under independent fair signs for 48 component scores. Equal component weights gave 73.8%. After removal of the first day, only 36 pairs remained and the exact probability was 0.0524. These results support a direction in selected magnitude order under the stated null, beyond a prior count-clustering endpoint. They do not identify direct triggering or a rupture mechanism. Revised mixed-scale catalog data, missed close events, fixed windows and component independence limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, an exact null distribution, a figure, source hashes and a separate numerical audit. External event records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Larger-first shares and conditional group bootstrap intervals, plus the exact primary signed-score null distribution. Independent symmetric component scores are assumed.
